title: Pushing a Koszul-regular immersion through a smooth morphism
statement: Let $Z,P,S$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $i:Z\to P$, $p:P\to S$ and $j:Z\to S$ be morphisms with $p\circ i=j$. Assume $p$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and both $i$ and $j$ are immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. If $i$ is Koszul-regular, then $j$ is Koszul-regular. Here an immersion is Koszul-regular if, locally at each source point, it is a closed immersion into an open subscheme of its target whose ideal is locally generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Sequence lengths may vary. No Noetherian, separation, or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: First prove the assertion when $P=\mathbf A^n_S$. Fix $z\in Z$. By the immersion hypothesis, shrink $S$ to an affine open on which $j$ is closed, and restrict $P,Z$ accordingly. Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, and $B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$. The affine description of a closed immersion and of affine space identifies $i$ with an $A$-algebra map $B\to A/I$. It is surjective because it contains the quotient map on constants. Lift the images of $x_l$ to $a_l\in A$, and put $t_l=x_l-a_l$, $K=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Evaluation at $a$ gives $B/K\cong A$ and identifies the kernel $J$ of $B\to A/I$ with $K+IB$: explicitly $f(x)-f(a)\in K$, and $f$ is in the kernel exactly when $f(a)\in I$.

Translation gives $B=A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. In $B/(t_1,\ldots,t_{l-1})$ multiplication by $t_l$ is injective by uniqueness of polynomial coefficients. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular] makes $(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$ Koszul-regular. The degree-one coefficients in the $t$ variables identify $K/K^2$ with $A^n$ and $K/KJ$ with $(A/I)^n$: modulo $KJ=K^2+IK$, precisely the linear coefficients modulo $I$ remain. Define $D:J/J^2\to(A/I)^n$ by the linear coefficients of $f$ modulo $I$. For $f,g\in J$, the linear coefficients of $fg$ are $f(a)$ times those of $g$ plus $g(a)$ times those of $f$, hence vanish modulo $I$; so $D$ is well-defined. Multiplication by $b\in B$ acts on these coefficients through $b(a)\bmod I$, proving $B/J$-linearity. The map $K/KJ\to J/J^2$ sends the standard basis to $[t_l]$, and $D([t_l])=e_l$. It is therefore split injective. Its cokernel is $J/(K+J^2)$ by the quotient definitions.

The hypothesis on $i$ and [lem-sfb-koszul-closed-immersion-affine-criterion] give, near every prime of $B$ containing $J$, principal neighbourhoods on which $J$ has finite Koszul-regular generators. The globally Koszul-regular generators $t_l$ of $K$ remain so after localization: $B\to B_h$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], so their images are Koszul-regular [lem-sc-koszul-regular-flat-base-change]. Apply [lem-sfb-koszul-split-conormal-cancellation] to $K\subseteq J$ using the split sequence just constructed. Its conclusion gives locally Koszul-regular generators for $J/K=I$ in $B/K=A$. Further principal localizations keep these generators Koszul-regular by the same two flatness citations, so the same affine criterion shows that $j$ is Koszul-regular. This proves the polynomial case for every $n\geq0$.

For general smooth $p$, fix $z\in Z$. Choose an affine open $V_0\subseteq S$ containing $j(z)$ on which $j$ is closed. Choose an affine neighbourhood $U_0\subseteq p^{-1}V_0$ of $i(z)$ on which $i$ is closed. In the closed subscheme $j^{-1}V_0\subseteq V_0$, the open neighbourhood $i^{-1}U_0$ is the inverse image of an open of $V_0$. Choose a principal open $V=D(a)\subseteq V_0$ containing $j(z)$ whose inverse image in $Z$ is contained in $i^{-1}U_0$. Then $U=U_0\cap p^{-1}V$ is principal affine in $U_0$, and $Z_V=j^{-1}V$ is closed in both $U$ and $V$. Restriction preserves smoothness [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. Write $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}C$. The affine smooth comparison [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], with [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], supplies a finite presentation $C=A[y_1,\ldots,y_m]/(g_1,\ldots,g_c)$, hence a closed $V$-immersion $h:U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^m_V$.

The polynomial projection $\mathbf A^m_V\to V$ is smooth [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], and $U\to V$ is smooth. Apply [lem-pur-smooth-pair-regular-immersion] to the closed immersion $h$. It gives regular generators for its ideal on affine neighbourhoods of every point of $U$. They are Koszul-regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular]. Consequently $h$ is Koszul-regular. Restricting the original $i$ preserves its Koszul regularity: intersect a regular-equation neighbourhood with $U$, refine by principal opens, and use that localization is flat [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat] and preserves Koszul regularity [lem-sc-koszul-regular-flat-base-change]. By [lem-sfb-koszul-immersion-composition], the composite $Z_V\to U\xrightarrow h\mathbf A^m_V$ is Koszul-regular. Apply the polynomial case of Steps 1--3 to this composite and its projection to $V$; it proves $Z_V\to V$ Koszul-regular. Since $z$ was arbitrary, the local definition proves the assertion for $j$.
